Print hub — paper companions

You’re already welcome here—take what helps, leave the rest. Paper is optional. KJV only, no pressure.

Most printable doors on the site point back here so you can find them again without hunting. Think of it as a drawer on the porch—open it when paper helps; leave it closed when today is only rest.

Family & Kids — parent doorway and on-device rhythm: Family hub; kids’ daily doorway: Kids Battle home; August–July pacing: Year-round rhythm; household armor and stories: Family Armor.

Think of these as scrap paper on the porch—there if you want them, no assignment attached. Print what fits the day; five quiet minutes still counts.

7-Day Emergency Calm Pack

A one-tap doorway for heavy weeks: one verse, one small step, one prayer each day, with printable companions for home, bedside, or travel.

Open the emergency calm pack — includes links to Calm, plans, and ready print sheets.

Printable Pack Generator

Build a themed companion in one calm step. The first three ready-made packs are Anxiety Anchor Pack, Bedtime Peace for Littles, and Grief Comfort Bundle — each with KJV verses, gentle breakdowns, writing space, and ink-friendly print layout.

Open the printable pack generator — print the pack as-is or save it as a PDF from your browser when you want a paper companion you can keep nearby.

Daily Rhythm Companions

Gentle structures to help you begin the day with the Lord and end it in peace — flexible for individuals, parents, and whole families.

  • One Week of Quiet Rhythm — A calm seven-day rhythm with morning quiet time, evening reflection, and a simple family table prompt. Spacious and flexible for anyone wanting gentle structure in their hand.
  • One Week of Quiet Rhythm – Kids & Family Edition — The same gentle rhythm, made simpler and more joyful for children and families. Larger fonts, drawing space, and light-hearted prompts that invite everyone to notice God together without pressure.
  • Be Still Moments — Five short, independent 5-minute cards (one for each weekday) with a single KJV verse and a quiet prompt. Ideal for busy mornings, lunch breaks, or any moment you simply need to pause and remember the Lord is near.
  • Evening in the University (one page) — Four KJV family evenings (Deuteronomy 6, Psalm 4, Luke 24, Matthew 11) on a single table-friendly sheet. Same text as Battle Plans → Evening in the University.
  • University at the Table (one page) — Four short KJV verses from the University quiet rooms (peace, rest, children taught of the Lord, rejoice in this day) and a calm one-minute family aloud—for the table, car, or bedside. No plan day counter; pairs with any University course on paper.
  • Morning & evening (two cards) — One page: Family Armor morning reset (Lamentations 3, Psalm 5) plus night 1 of Evening in the University; full four-night sheet for nights 2–4.
  • One week in the University — Seven days on one page: the same short morning + evening lights from the two-card sheet and the four-night print (with gentle “echo” evenings on days 5–7). Evening · plan.
  • University of Comparison (one page) — All six KJV days on one sheet; same text as Battle Plans → Comparison.
  • University of Anger (one page) — Six days of anchor verses on a single table-friendly page; full plan on the device for each day’s step and prayer.
  • University of Regret (one page) — Six KJV days on one sheet—burden, contrition, pressing forward, no condemnation; Battle Plans for the full week.
  • Contentment in Small Seasons (one page) — Six KJV days when ordinary feels heavy—sufficient day, learned contentment, labor as gift, small things, quiet soul, His nearness; Battle Plans for each day’s step.
  • University of Overwhelm (one page) — Six KJV days when too much lands together—path known, comforts, casting care, perplexed-not-desperate, wait-only soul; Battle Plans for steps and prayers.
  • Fear for My Children — University (one page) — Six KJV days for parental vigil—Father’s will toward little ones, peace on taught children, welcoming hands, trust naming fear, courageous spirit, confidence in Christ’s finishing work; Battle Plans on the device.
  • When the year feels heavy (one page) — Five KJV anchor verses—mercies new, thanks, all things, strength to wait—for New Year’s Eve or early January. Pairs with Gentle New Year reset or New Year week on the device.
  • Gentle New Year week (seven days) — Seven KJV days on one sheet, matching New Year Week — Steady Mercies; follows naturally from the five-verse “heavy year” page when you want the full week in ink.
  • Winter comfort read-alouds (one page) — Four family tells—storm (Mark 4:37–39), still waters (Psalm 23:1–2), long nights (Psalm 119:147–148), and the return home (Luke 15:20–24)—on one or two letter-size sheets, margins minimum. A one-verse “cast thy burden” line (Psalm 55:22) stays on the site and map, not on this print. Same family as Simple family rhythm → winter.
  • When school feels hard (one page) — Five KJV verses for a rough day at school—kids and parents. Pairs with Back to school in the University and Come unto me on Family rhythm; fall read-alouds when you have a table before you print.
  • When the days grow short (one page) — Five KJV verses for late November and early December—mercies, wisdom, comfort, light, a lamp. Pairs with late autumn read-alouds and Seasonal → late fall, quiet winter.
  • Year-end rest (one page) — Five KJV verses for the last nights of December and New Year’s Eve—peace, yoke, care, rest. Pairs with December manger read-alouds, Advent & Christmas in the University, and Seasonal → New Year.
  • Quiet New Year reset (one page) — Five KJV verses matching Gentle New Year reset—mercies, wisdom, seasons, new creature, press forward. Gentle companion to year-end rest; the full John 1:1–14 read-aloud on Family rhythm and the University map when the table has time.
  • When winter lingers (one page) — Five KJV verses for cold, gray weeks after the new year—wait, courage, look to the Lord. Pairs with late fall, quiet winter and the full Good Shepherd read (John 10:1–18) on Family rhythm; map mirror: University → Shepherd, door to fold.
  • Spring at the table (one page) — Five KJV verses for March and early spring—winter past, word that does not return void, joy in the morning, new mercies, go out with joy. Pairs with let the little children come and Resurrection Hope on the device; map mirror: University → let the little children come.
  • When spring feels overwhelming (one page) — Five KJV verses for longer days, pollen season, and weeks that outrun your rest—sufficient to the day, peace, one care, sleep, unhurried growth. Pairs with the lost piece (Luke 15) on Family rhythm; map mirror: University → the lost piece; Evening in the University when the table needs a slow lane.
  • When spring feels scattered (one page) — Five KJV verses for busy minds and broken focus—seek first, one thing, trust and direction, things above, one desire. Pairs with the full read your Father knows (Matthew 6:25–34); map mirror: University → same read; overwhelming (one page) when the week tires the body as well as the mind.
  • When summer feels too much (one page) — Five KJV verses for heat, full calendars, and everyone-home-at-once days—come apart, wait, overcome, good and quiet, soul stayed. Pairs with the sower and good soil (full, Matthew 13:1–9; 18–23); map mirror: University → sower, full; Summer stillness on the device.
  • Late summer reset (one page) — Five KJV verses for the slower in-between weeks before school ramps—come to Christ, thanksgiving prayer, new mercies, cast care, wait and renew. Pairs with peace, be still (full, Mark 4), cast all your care (1 Peter 5), and late summer, early rest on the device; map: summer & harvest.
  • When the leaves start turning (one page) — Five KJV verses for the shift from summer into fall—seasons, tree by the waters, the Word that abides, no shadow of turning, inward day by day. Pairs with lost sheep (full, Luke 15), washed their feet (John 13); map: back to school; quiet fall harvest on the device.
  • When fall feels heavy (one page) — Five KJV verses for busier, darker fall weeks—hope in God, new mercies, power to the faint, not crushed, peace. Pairs with October: thanks, one loaf (Family rhythm) and October at the table (map); when the days grow short for November dusk; Harvest Gratitude (7 days) on the device.
  • When Thanksgiving feels lonely or hard (one page) — Five KJV verses for a thin, loud, or far-from-home holiday table—He draws near, comfort, not forsaken, the mourner’s hope, thanks with your requests. Pairs with November: widow, give thanks (Family rhythm) and November at the table (map); Seasonal → lonely or hard Thanksgiving when you want the room, not just the sheet.
  • As the year ends (one page) — Five KJV verses for the last days of December—number our days, strength for the day, crown of goodness, Christ the same, good work to the day of Christ. Complements year-end rest (one page) (peace, yoke, care); pairs with December manger reads (Family rhythm) and Seasonal → as the year ends.
  • Start the year in the Word — one hub for January: New Year prints (including quiet New Year reset), New Year week, Gentle New Year reset, and Emmanuel week, plus a short list of steady verses and John’s prologue (full read).

Memory Verse Activities

Simple, ink-friendly worksheets for hiding Scripture in your heart. One verse per sheet with space to write, draw, or copy the KJV text. Perfect for individuals, families, or homeschool.

Family Armor Checklist

Weekly checklist for putting on the full armor of God together (Ephesians 6). Space for each family member to note one way they saw God’s protection that week. Calm, reverent, no pressure.

KJV English only for now — Spanish and other languages coming when the Lord leads.
